text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Necessary preconditions have been met for further growth of production, exports and earnings in the country, say experts at a seminar of Serbian chamber of commerce.
- Total dinar deposits stood at 76 million dinars ($15 million) on August 31, which is four million dinars less than in July.
- Yugoslavia's potential for producing mineral water stands at 15 billion liters, 90 percent of which could be exported, it was pointed out at a seminar in Arandjelovac.
- Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Nikola Sainovic and Serbian interior minister Zoran Sokolovic promise to maintain security in Kosovo following latest terrorist act in which two Serbs were killed.
- The crime rate is down and efficiency is up in fight against economic crime, says Serbian deputy interior minister Radovan Stojicic.
- Management of Zastava arms and trade union representatives have reached an agreement and the workers do not need to continue their protsets, president of the Zastava group Srboljub Vasovic said.
- Opposition in Serbian town of Nis demands representation on local electoral board and threatens to block elections if its demands are not met.
- Belgrade public transport drivers' trade union will stage a strike Monday if the authorities do not start negotiations with its representatives.
- Serbian lawyers will strike from Monday Oct 28 to Oct 30 because their demands over lowering taxes have not been met.
- First sales and service centre for Toyota cars opens in Yugoslavia (Serbia, Montenegro).
- Introduction of trolleys in city transport is a big chance for the Smederevo wagon producer Gosa, says director Branislav Milanovic. -- Belgrade newsroom 381 11 222 42 54
